Arroyo calls close()/join() on the old strategy at each rebalance, and SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close() calls queue_pool.shutdown(), which sets the workers' shutdown flag and shuts down every queue. The next strategy reuses the dead pool. queue.put() raises ShutDown, which submit() catches and logs, then it marks the offset complete. The messages are silently dropped and their offsets get committed. The OffsetTracker also keeps stale last_committed and offset state from the revoked assignment.

Commit called from a background thread; stale offsets kept across rebalances
The commit function is invoked from a separate daemon thread, but Arroyo's commit callback is meant to be called from the consumer thread and is not thread-safe. The OffsetTracker is also never reset on rebalance, so offsets for revoked partitions may be committed later.

Commit stalls permanently on any offset gap
The contiguity check requires every offset between last_committed+1 and max to be in all_offsets. Legitimate gaps (compacted or transactional topics, offsets skipped after a rebalance rewind) are never filled. Committing stalls and all_offsets grows without bound.
